teile.einleitung: The Taizé Community is a Christian community of brothers in a small village in Burgundy, France. It was founded by the Swiss Brother Roger. Every year tens of thousands of young people come there from all over the world.
wichtigste: Taizé is in Burgundy in France, not far from Cluny.
The community was founded by Brother Roger, who came from Switzerland.
Protestant and Catholic brothers from many countries live together.
The Taizé songs are short and are often repeated.
Since 1978 there have been European Youth Meetings over the New Year.
In 2017/2018 the youth meeting took place in Basel.
Since December 2023 Brother Matthew has led the community.

abschnitte.text: **Brother Roger** was born in Switzerland in 1915, the son of a Reformed pastor. In 1940 he came to the village of **Taizé** in Burgundy. There he wanted to found a community in which people live together in prayer and reconciliation. Soon more brothers joined him. In 2005 he was attacked during evening prayer in the church by a mentally ill woman and died shortly afterwards.

What is special about Taizé is that **Protestant and Catholic brothers** from many countries live together. The community is a sign of **ecumenism**, that is, of understanding between the churches. The brothers earn their own living and do not accept gifts for themselves. After Brother Roger, **Brother Alois** led the community, and since December 2023 **Brother Matthew** from Great Britain has been the prior.

Taizé is well known for its **chants**. They consist of short verses that are **repeated** many times. This means everyone can join in quickly, even if they do not know the language well. A calm, meditative mood arises. The songs are sung in many languages and are now widespread in churches all over the world.

abschnitte.titel: Young people from all over the world
abschnitte.text: Every year many young people travel to Taizé and spend a week there with prayer, conversations and simple work. In 1982 the **Pilgrimage of Trust on Earth** began. It invites young people to work for peace and reconciliation in everyday life. This also includes the large meetings in other countries.

Since 1978 Taizé has invited people to a **European Youth Meeting** in a large city **over the New Year**. The guests usually stay with **host families**. Over the New Year of 2017/2018 the meeting took place in **Basel**. Well over 15,000 young people came, and many stayed with families in the region, including in Germany and France.

gewusst: Brother Roger came from Provence in the canton of Vaud.
In Taizé the guests eat very simply, often from one bowl and with only a spoon.

teile.einleitung: The Roman Catholic Church in Switzerland is divided into dioceses. A diocese is an area led by a bishop. In Switzerland there are six dioceses and two territorial abbeys.
wichtigste: Switzerland has six dioceses: Basel, Chur, Lausanne-Geneva-Fribourg, Lugano, St Gallen and Sion.
The episcopal seat of the Diocese of Basel is in Solothurn.
With ten cantons, the Diocese of Basel is the largest in area.
The Diocese of Lugano covers the canton of Ticino, the Diocese of Sion the Valais.
Einsiedeln and Saint-Maurice are territorial abbeys.
Together the bishops form the Swiss Bishops' Conference.

abschnitte.text: A **diocese** is an area of the Catholic Church that is led by a **bishop**. Many parishes belong to a diocese. The main church of a diocese is called the **cathedral**. There stands the bishop's chair, the cathedra, after which the church is named. In Switzerland there are **six dioceses**.

The **Diocese of Basel**, with **ten cantons**, is the largest in Switzerland in area. Its episcopal seat, however, is not in Basel but in **Solothurn**, in the Cathedral of St Ursus. The **Diocese of Chur** covers, among other areas, Graubünden, Zurich and parts of Central Switzerland. It is regarded as the oldest diocese in Switzerland. The **Diocese of St Gallen** covers the two cantons of St Gallen and Appenzell.

The **Diocese of Lausanne, Geneva and Fribourg** has its episcopal seat in **Fribourg**. The **Diocese of Sion** covers the canton of **Valais**. To the **Diocese of Lugano** belongs the whole canton of **Ticino**. In this way the dioceses also reflect the language regions of Switzerland: German, French and Italian.

Two monasteries are not subject to any diocese: **Einsiedeln** and **Saint-Maurice**. They are **territorial abbeys**. Their abbot leads a small territory in a way similar to a bishop. Saint-Maurice in Valais is regarded as one of the oldest monasteries of the West to have existed without a break. Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz is a well-known place of pilgrimage.

The Swiss bishops work together in the **Swiss Bishops' Conference**. There they discuss common questions and speak for the Catholic Church in the whole country. Besides the dioceses, in many cantons there are church corporations. These administer the church taxes and are elected democratically by the members.

gewusst: The dioceses of Switzerland are directly subject to the pope and belong to no church province with an archbishop.
The Christian Catholic Church has a diocese of its own with its seat in Bern.

teile.einleitung: The Baroque is an art style that was widespread in Europe from about 1600 to 1750. Typical are splendid churches and palaces with a lot of gold, movement and light. In Switzerland too there are famous Baroque buildings.
wichtigste: The word “Baroque” probably comes from a word for an irregularly shaped pearl.
The Counter-Reformation encouraged the building of splendid Baroque churches.
The Jesuit church Il Gesù in Rome became a model for many Baroque churches.
The master builder Francesco Borromini came from Ticino.
Gian Lorenzo Bernini created the bronze canopy in St Peter's Basilica.
The Abbey Precinct of St Gallen has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.

abschnitte.text: The name **Baroque** probably comes from the Portuguese word for an **irregularly shaped pearl**. At first this was meant as an insult: critics found the style overloaded and crooked. Today it is admired for its splendour. Typical are curving forms, lots of decoration, gold, marble and a strong play of **light and shadow**.

After the Reformation the Catholic Church wanted to inspire and strengthen its faithful. This movement is called the **Counter-Reformation**. Splendid churches were meant to give a foretaste of heaven. A model for many Baroque churches became the Jesuit church **Il Gesù** in Rome. The Jesuit order built similar churches in many countries.

In Rome worked the most famous Baroque artists. **Gian Lorenzo Bernini** created the great bronze **canopy** over the papal altar in St Peter's Basilica. His rival **Francesco Borromini** came from what is now the canton of **Ticino**. He built churches with unusual, curving ground plans. Many master builders from Ticino worked all over Europe at that time.

From **1719** the master builder **Kaspar Moosbrugger** erected the Baroque abbey church of **Einsiedeln** in the canton of Schwyz. Another masterpiece is the **Abbey Precinct of St Gallen** with its late Baroque cathedral and the famous Abbey Library. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since **1983**. In Bavaria the **Wieskirche** by Dominikus Zimmermann is also a World Heritage Site.

Baroque painters painted ceilings in such a way that you think you see an **open sky** or a high dome. This technique is called **trompe-l'oeil**, in English “deceive the eye”. Angels and saints seem to float in the clouds. The Baroque exists in music too: Johann Sebastian Bach and George Frideric Handel are well-known Baroque composers.

gewusst: In the church of Sant'Ignazio in Rome the dome is only painted: from one particular point it looks deceptively real.
The Abbey Library of St Gallen is one of the oldest libraries in the world and holds very old manuscripts.

teile.einleitung: The First Council of Nicaea was a great assembly of bishops in the year 325. Emperor Constantine had summoned it. There an important dispute about Jesus Christ was decided.
wichtigste: The council took place in Nicaea in the year 325.
Emperor Constantine summoned it.
It is regarded as the first ecumenical council.
About 300 bishops took part.
It decided that the Son is of the same substance as the Father.
The date of Easter was also settled uniformly.
Nicaea is now called Iznik and lies in Turkey.

abschnitte.text: Emperor **Constantine** had supported Christianity in the Roman Empire. He wanted the Church to be united, since a united Church was also meant to hold the empire together. So he invited the bishops to **Nicaea** and paid for their journey. The city lies in the north-west of present-day Turkey and is now called **Iznik**. About 300 bishops came, most of them from the east of the empire.

At the centre was the priest **Arius** of Alexandria in Egypt. He taught that the Son of God was created and subordinate to the Father. This teaching is called **Arianism**. Many bishops contradicted him fiercely. An important opponent was the young deacon **Athanasius**, who later became bishop of Alexandria.

The council decided that the Son is **of one substance** with the Father. In Greek this is “homoousios”. This means: the Son is just as much God as the Father and is not created. This sentence went into a creed. Arius and his followers were condemned. But the dispute went on for many more years afterwards.

The council also settled the **date of Easter**. Easter was to be celebrated on the same day everywhere in the Church, and on a Sunday. To this day the calculation of Easter is linked to the beginning of spring and the full moon.

An **ecumenical council** is an assembly of bishops from the whole Church. Nicaea is regarded as the first of these councils. It is recognised by the Catholic and Orthodox churches and by most Protestant churches. The creed that goes back to Nicaea is still spoken in many churches today.

gewusst: According to an old tradition, there were exactly 318 bishops at Nicaea.
In 2025 many churches marked the 1700th anniversary of the council.

teile.einleitung: German mysticism is a spiritual movement of the Middle Ages. Mystics sought a very close, personal experience of God. Many of them no longer wrote only in Latin but also in German.
wichtigste: Mysticism means the search for a direct experience of God.
Mechthild of Magdeburg wrote “The Flowing Light of the Godhead”.
Important mystics were the Dominicans Meister Eckhart, Johannes Tauler and Heinrich Seuse.
Elsbeth Stagel from the convent of Töss near Winterthur recorded conversations with Seuse.
Niklaus von Flüe in the Ranft is regarded as the best-known mystic of Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The word **mysticism** comes from Greek and has to do with “hidden”. Mystics wanted to know God not only through teaching but to **experience him inwardly**. They prayed a great deal, lived simply and described their experiences. Especially in the 13th and 14th centuries they also wrote in **German**. In this way they contributed a great deal to the development of the German language.

**Mechthild of Magdeburg** lived as a beguine in Magdeburg and later in the convent of Helfta. Her work **“The Flowing Light of the Godhead”** is among the earliest mystical writings in German. Three Dominicans are also very well known: **Meister Eckhart**, **Johannes Tauler** and **Heinrich Seuse**. They often preached to nuns and wrote about life with God.

In the Dominican convent of **Töss** near Winterthur lived **Elsbeth Stagel**. She was a spiritual pupil of Heinrich Seuse and collected his letters and accounts. She also wrote biographies of sisters from Töss. The best-known mystic of Switzerland is regarded as **Niklaus von Flüe**. From 1467 he lived as a hermit in the **Ranft** in Obwalden, was canonised in 1947 and is regarded as the patron saint of Switzerland.

gewusst: In Switzerland, Niklaus von Flüe is often called “Brother Klaus”.
We still use many words that the mystics coined today, for example “Gelassenheit” (composure).

teile.einleitung: The five books of Moses stand right at the beginning of the Bible. In Judaism they are called the **Torah**, in scholarship often the **Pentateuch**, which is Greek and means “five books”. They tell the story from the creation of the world to the death of Moses.
wichtigste: The five books are called Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy.
In Judaism they are called the Torah, which means instruction or teaching.
Genesis begins with the creation of the world.
Exodus tells of the Israelites' departure from Egypt.
Leviticus contains many rules for priests and sacrifices.
At the end Moses dies on Mount Nebo, looking into the promised land.

abschnitte.text: The first book is called **Genesis**, which means origin or beginning. It begins with the creation of the world in six days and a day of rest. After that come well-known stories such as Adam and Eve, Noah and the Flood, or the Tower of Babel. Later God calls **Abraham** from his homeland to a new country and promises him many descendants. Abraham is regarded as the forefather of Judaism, Christianity and Islam.

The second book is called **Exodus**, which means departure. The Israelites live as slaves in Egypt. With God's help Moses leads them to freedom. At Mount Sinai the people receive the **Ten Commandments**. This story is especially important for Judaism and is told every year at the festival of Passover.

The third book, **Leviticus**, is named after the tribe of Levi, from which the priests came. It contains rules for worship, sacrifices and purity. The fourth book is called **Numbers**. The name comes from the fact that the people of Israel are counted in it. After that it tells of the long journey through the desert.

abschnitte.titel: Deuteronomy and the death of Moses
abschnitte.text: The fifth book is called **Deuteronomy**, which means “second law”. In it Moses repeats the commandments once more for the people before he dies. From **Mount Nebo** he is allowed to see the promised land, but not to enter it. There he dies at the age of 120. With this the five books of Moses end.

For Jews, the **Torah** is the most important part of Scripture. In the synagogue it is read aloud from a handwritten **scroll**. Over the course of a year it is read through completely, section by section. For Christians too, the five books of Moses are part of the Bible, namely the beginning of the Old Testament.

gewusst: A Torah scroll is written by hand with quill and ink on parchment, which can take over a year.
The Greek names of the five books come from an old Greek translation of the Bible.

teile.einleitung: Lent is the period of preparation for Easter. It lasts 40 days. In this time many Christians give something up and think of people in need.
wichtigste: Lent lasts 40 days.
It recalls that Jesus fasted in the wilderness.
In this time many people give up sweets, for example.
The priest's vestment is purple during Lent.
The Alleluia is not sung in the Catholic Mass.
The last week of Lent is called Holy Week.

abschnitte.text: **Lent** begins on Ash Wednesday and lasts **40 days**. Sundays are not counted. The number recalls that **Jesus**, according to the Bible, fasted for 40 days in the wilderness. The people of Israel were also on their way for 40 years in the desert.

In the past, people gave up meat and other foods during Lent. Today many people give up **sweets**, television or their mobile phone. By giving something up, you are meant to have more time for God and for other people. It is also about becoming aware of what is really important.

During Lent the priest wears a **purple** vestment. Purple is the colour of penance and reflection. Catholics do not sing the joyful **Alleluia** in this season. It is heard again only at the Easter Vigil. In some churches a **Lenten veil** (Hungertuch) hangs in front of the altar. It often shows pictures from the Bible and from the lives of poor people.

During Lent many Swiss parishes and church congregations invite people to a **soup day**. People eat a simple **soup** together and donate the money they would have spent on a bigger meal. The donations go to aid organisations. The Catholic Fastenaktion and the Reformed HEKS run a joint campaign on this every year.

The last week of Lent is called **Holy Week**. It begins with Palm Sunday. On Maundy Thursday people remember the last meal of Jesus, on Good Friday his death. After that, Christians celebrate his resurrection at Easter.

gewusst: The “Kar” in the German word Karwoche comes from Old High German “kara” and means lament or mourning.
Lent is also called the Passion season or Quadragesima, which means “the fortieth day”.

teile.einleitung: The Cluniac Reform was one of the most important movements of renewal in the Church in the Middle Ages. It started from the monastery of Cluny in Burgundy. Monks wanted to live strictly by their rule again and to free the Church from worldly influence.
wichtigste: The monastery of Cluny was founded in 910 and followed the Rule of Benedict.
It was endowed by Duke William I of Aquitaine.
Cluny was placed directly under the Pope and so protected from the nobility.
The first abbot was called Berno, followed by Odo.
The reformers fought against simony, the trade in church offices.
The third abbey church was the largest church in Christendom for centuries.
Romainmôtier in the canton of Vaud also belonged to the Cluniac network.

abschnitte.text: In the year **910**, **Duke William I of Aquitaine**, known as the Pious, gave land for a new monastery at **Cluny** in Burgundy. In the deed of foundation he gave up any influence of his own. The monastery was placed under the apostle Peter, and so directly under the **Pope**. This meant that neither nobles nor local bishops could make decisions about it. The monks lived by the **Rule of Benedict**.

The first abbot was **Berno**, who had already led other monasteries. He was followed in 927 by **Odo**, under whom the reform spread widely. Cluny was lucky to have several capable abbots one after another, who ruled for a long time. They reformed many monasteries all over Europe. The monks placed great value on solemn services and prayers.

In the Middle Ages some people bought church offices with money. This is called **simony**, after Simon Magus, who according to the Acts of the Apostles wanted to buy spiritual powers. The reformers fought against this trade. They wanted clergy to lead a devout life. The ideas from Cluny later also influenced the popes, who resisted the influence of kings on the Church.

abschnitte.titel: The huge church of Cluny III
abschnitte.text: From **1088** the monks built a new abbey church, called **Cluny III**. It was about **187 metres** long and for centuries it was the **largest church in Christendom**. Only the new building of St Peter's in Rome surpassed it. After the French Revolution, most of the church was demolished. Today only a small remnant stands.

The network of monasteries was strictly organised: at the top stood only the **Abbot of Cluny**, and the dependent houses were called **priories** and were led by priors. In western Switzerland, **Romainmôtier** in the canton of Vaud belonged to it, and its Romanesque church is still preserved today. The monastery of **Payerne** in the canton of Vaud was also linked with Cluny. You can still visit its large abbey church today.

gewusst: At its height, more than a thousand monasteries all over Europe belonged to the Cluniac network.
Only a few kilometres from Cluny lies the village of Taizé with its well-known community of brothers.

teile.einleitung: Caritas Switzerland is a Catholic aid organisation. It works above all against poverty, in Switzerland and in other countries. The name comes from the Latin word for charity, or love of one's neighbour.
wichtigste: Caritas Switzerland works especially against poverty.
The word “Caritas” is Latin and means love of one's neighbour.
Caritas Switzerland works together with 16 regional Caritas organisations.
In Caritas shops, people with little money can shop at low prices.
The KulturLegi makes culture and sport cheaper for people on low incomes.
The worldwide association is called Caritas Internationalis.

abschnitte.text: The Latin word **Caritas** means **love of one's neighbour**. Caritas Switzerland is an aid organisation that grew out of the Catholic Church. It was founded in 1901 and is based in **Lucerne**. Its help is for all people in need, whatever their religion. Caritas works especially **against poverty**.

Caritas Switzerland works together with **16 regional Caritas organisations**. They operate in different cantons and know the situation on the ground. They advise people who have debts or are short of money. They also offer support for families and help with integration. Many volunteers help out.

In a **Caritas shop**, **people with little money** can do their shopping. For this you need a shopping card, which you get from a social services office. Food and everyday goods there are much cheaper than in ordinary shops. Often these are goods that would otherwise have been left over. So less is thrown away at the same time.

Even people with little money should be able to go to a museum, the cinema or the swimming pool. That is why Caritas has the **KulturLegi**. With this card you get **cheaper culture and sport**, courses and leisure activities. This way everyone can take part in social life. Many providers all over Switzerland join in.

Caritas Switzerland also helps abroad, for example after natural disasters or in poor regions. There are Caritas organisations in many countries around the world. They are united in the association **Caritas Internationalis**, which is based in Rome. Together they can help quickly after major disasters.

gewusst: Every year Caritas Switzerland draws attention to poverty in Switzerland with reports and campaigns.
The Protestant churches also have their own aid organisations that take on similar tasks.

teile.einleitung: Eiertütschen, or egg tapping, is a popular Easter custom in Switzerland. Two people knock their hard-boiled Easter eggs against each other. Whoever's egg stays whole has won.
wichtigste: In egg tapping, two people knock their Easter eggs together.
The winner is the person whose egg stays whole.
Usually you tap with the pointed end first.
By old custom the winner got the broken egg.
In Bern people meet at Easter on the Kornhausplatz for egg tapping.
At the Zwänzgerle in Zurich, adults throw twenty-rappen coins at the children's eggs.

abschnitte.text: In **egg tapping** each person takes a **hard-boiled** Easter egg. You hold the egg in your fist and let only the **point** show. Then one person knocks their egg against the other's egg. The egg with the harder shell stays **whole**, and its owner has won. After that you can often go on tapping with the round end.

By **old custom** the winner was allowed to keep the other person's broken egg. Someone who tapped well could collect many eggs that way. Today everyone usually keeps their own egg and eats it afterwards. Some people believe that certain eggs have particularly hard shells. But there is no sure recipe for winning; it also takes some **luck**.

In **Bern**, on **Easter Sunday**, many people meet on the **Kornhausplatz** for egg tapping. Families, children and adults tap their eggs together there. The custom has been recorded in the square for over 100 years. For many people this visit is a fixed part of the Easter festival.

In **Zurich** there is a different Easter custom, the **Zwänzgerle**. It takes place on **Easter Monday** in the old town at the Haus zum Rüden on the Limmat. Children hold out their Easter eggs, and adults throw a **Zwänzgi**, that is, a 20-rappen coin, at them. If the coin sticks in the egg, the adult gets the egg. If it falls off, the child may keep the coin.

gewusst: The word “tütschen” is dialect and means roughly “to knock” or “to bang together”.
Dyeing eggs is a very old Easter custom, in the past often done with onion skins.

teile.einleitung: Felix Manz was a scholar from Zurich and one of the first Anabaptists. The Anabaptists baptised only adults who had consciously decided for the faith. Felix Manz was drowned in the Limmat in 1527.
wichtigste: Felix Manz lived in Zurich at the time of the Reformation.
He was a particularly respected expert in Hebrew.
On 21 January 1525, the first believers' baptism took place in the house of the Manz family on Neustadtgasse.
He was the first Anabaptist to be executed by a Reformed authority.
Since 2004 a memorial plaque on the Schipfe by the Limmat has recalled him.

abschnitte.text: Felix Manz came from Zurich. He had studied well and was a particularly respected expert in the **Hebrew** language, in which the Old Testament is written. At first he supported the Reformation of **Huldrych Zwingli**. With other young men he read the Bible closely. Soon they felt that Zwingli did not go far enough.

Manz and his friends held that only those who believe for themselves should be baptised. That is why they rejected the baptism of children. According to tradition, on **21 January 1525** the first **believers' baptism** took place in the house of the Manz family on **Neustadtgasse**. This is regarded as the beginning of the **Anabaptist movement**. The Anabaptists called themselves brothers, while their opponents called them rebaptisers.

The Zurich authorities banned the Anabaptists and had them persecuted. Manz was arrested several times. On 5 January 1527 he was drowned in the **Limmat**. He was the first Anabaptist to be executed by a Reformed authority. Since **2004**, a **memorial plaque** on the **Schipfe** by the Limmat has recalled him and other Anabaptists. Today the descendants of the Anabaptists live on, for example, among the Mennonites and the Amish.

gewusst: In 2004 the Reformed Church of Zurich invited descendants of the Anabaptists to a reconciliation meeting.

teile.einleitung: The Bible was not written in English but in ancient languages. The Old Testament arose mainly in Hebrew, the New Testament in Greek. Later the Bible was translated into a great many languages.
wichtigste: Most of the Old Testament is written in Hebrew.
Some parts are written in Aramaic.
The writings of the New Testament were composed in Greek.
Hebrew is written from right to left.
The ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament is called the Septuagint.
The Latin translation, the Vulgate, goes back mainly to Jerome.
The word “Bible” comes from the Greek word for “books”.

abschnitte.text: Most of the **Old Testament** is written in **Hebrew**, the language of the ancient people of Israel. Hebrew is written **from right to left**. In the original script the **vowels** were missing: only the consonants were written. Only in the Middle Ages did Jewish scholars, the Masoretes, add signs for the vowels. Some passages, for example in the Book of Daniel, are composed in **Aramaic**.

The writings of the **New Testament** were composed in **Greek**. It was a simple form of Greek that was understood all around the Mediterranean at that time. Jesus himself probably spoke **Aramaic** in everyday life. Because many Jews outside Israel spoke Greek, the Old Testament too was translated into Greek early on. This translation is called the **Septuagint**.

In the west of the Roman Empire people spoke **Latin**. At the end of the 4th century the scholar **Jerome** created a new Latin translation. It is called the **Vulgate**, which means “the commonly used one”. For over a thousand years it was the most important Bible of the Church in the West. Services were also celebrated in Latin.

At the time of the Reformation people wanted everyone to be able to read the Bible in their own language. **Martin Luther** translated it into German. In Zurich the **Zurich Bible** came about under **Huldrych Zwingli** and his colleagues. Today the Bible has been translated wholly or in part into more languages than any other book.

gewusst: The word “Bible” comes from the Greek “biblia”, “books”. So the Bible is really a whole library.
The name Septuagint means “seventy”. A legend tells that about seventy scholars made the translation.

teile.einleitung: Eschatology is a part of Christian theology. It asks what happens at the end of time and after death. This includes subjects such as the return of Christ, the Last Judgement and eternal life.
wichtigste: Eschatology means “the teaching of the last things”.
The expected return of Christ is called the Parousia.
According to Catholic teaching there is purgatory as a state of purification.
Chiliasm expects a thousand-year reign of Christ on earth.
Origen is linked with the teaching of universal reconciliation.
According to Catholic teaching the blessed attain the visio beatifica, the vision of God.

abschnitte.text: The word **eschatology** comes from Greek. “Eschatos” means “the last”. Eschatology is therefore the **teaching of the last things**. It deals with death, judgement, heaven and the end of the world. Judaism and Islam also have such teachings.

Christians expect that Jesus Christ will return at the end of time. This return is called the **Parousia**. Then the **Last Judgement** is to take place. In the Middle Ages the Latin sequence **“Dies irae”**, meaning “Day of Wrath”, arose about this. It was long sung in the funeral Mass and set to music by many composers.

According to Catholic teaching there is **purgatory**. It is a state of purification after death. The Protestant churches reject this teaching. According to the bull “Benedictus Deus” of 1336, the blessed in heaven attain the **visio beatifica**. This is the direct vision of God.

**Chiliasm** expects a thousand-year reign of Christ on earth. The word comes from the Greek word for a thousand. The Church Father **Origen** is linked with the teaching of **universal reconciliation**, in Greek apokatastasis. It says that in the end all will be reconciled with God. The Church later rejected this teaching.

The theologian **Albert Schweitzer** put forward “consistent eschatology”. He thought that Jesus had expected the early end of the world. Schweitzer later worked as a doctor in Lambaréné in Africa. The Basel theologian **Karl Barth** wrote in 1922 that a Christianity that is not wholly eschatology has nothing to do with Christ.

gewusst: The “Dies irae” appears in Mozart's famous Requiem.
Albert Schweitzer received the Nobel Peace Prize for his work as a doctor.

teile.einleitung: The Barmen Theological Declaration is an important confession of the Protestant church in Germany. It was adopted in 1934, when the National Socialists were in power. In it, Christians resisted the state determining the Church.
wichtigste: The declaration was adopted in 1934 in Barmen, today part of Wuppertal.
It was adopted by the first Confessing Synod of the German Evangelical Church.
It was directed against the “German Christians”.
It consists of six theses.
The most important draft was written by the Swiss theologian Karl Barth.
Lutherans, Reformed and United Christians supported it together.

abschnitte.text: In 1933 the **National Socialists** came to power in Germany. In the Protestant church there was the group of the **German Christians**. They wanted to join Christianity and National Socialism and to align the Church with the will of the state. Many pastors and congregations were against this. They joined together in the **Confessing Church**.

At the end of May 1934, representatives of these congregations met in **Barmen**, today a district of Wuppertal. It was the **first Confessing Synod** of the German Evangelical Church. There **Lutherans, Reformed and United Christians** came together, who otherwise had separate confessions. Together they adopted the Barmen Theological Declaration.

The declaration consists of **six theses**. The first thesis states: **Jesus Christ is the one Word of God** that the Church is to listen to. Alongside it there may be no other powers that the Church must obey. The theses also say that the state may not decide over faith. Each thesis first gives a Bible verse and then a rejection of false teachings.

The most important draft was written by **Karl Barth**. He was a **Swiss** Reformed theologian from Basel and was then teaching in Germany. Because he refused to swear the oath of loyalty to Hitler without reservation, he lost his post in 1935. After that he taught in **Basel**. Barth is regarded as one of the most important theologians of the 20th century.

The Barmen Declaration is regarded as a courageous sign of church resistance. Many Protestant churches have included it in their constitutions. From today's point of view, however, it is often reproached for having **kept silent about the persecution of the Jews**. It defended above all the freedom of the Church, not the rights of all persecuted people.

gewusst: The Barmen Declaration is one of the few confessions that Lutherans and Reformed Christians have supported together.
The synod met in the Gemarke Church, a Reformed church in Barmen.

teile.einleitung: Francis was Pope of the Catholic Church from 2013 to 2025. His real name was Jorge Mario Bergoglio, and he came from Argentina. He was known for his simple way of life and his commitment to the poor and the environment.
wichtigste: Jorge Mario Bergoglio was elected Pope in 2013.
His predecessor Benedict XVI had resigned of his own free will.
Francis lived in the Santa Marta guest house instead of the Apostolic Palace.
His encyclical “Laudato si'” of 2015 deals with the environment and creation.
“Fratelli tutti” of 2020 is about brotherhood among all people.
In 2018 he visited Geneva.
He died in 2025 and was buried in Santa Maria Maggiore.

abschnitte.text: **Jorge Mario Bergoglio** was born in 1936 in Buenos Aires in **Argentina**. He became a Jesuit and later Archbishop of Buenos Aires. In **2013**, Pope **Benedict XVI** resigned of his own free will. After that the cardinals elected Bergoglio Pope. He was the first Pope from the Americas and the first Jesuit in this office. He chose his name after **Francis of Assisi**.

Francis did not move into the magnificent **Apostolic Palace**. He lived in the **Santa Marta guest house** in the Vatican, where other clergy also live. He drove smaller cars and wore simple clothes. Again and again he called on the Church to care for the **poor**, the sick and refugees.

An **encyclical** is an important circular letter from the Pope. In **“Laudato si'”** of 2015, Francis wrote about the **environment and creation**. He called on people to protect the Earth as our “common home”. The title comes from the Canticle of the Sun by Francis of Assisi. In **“Fratelli tutti”** of 2020 he wrote about brotherhood and friendship among all people.

In **2018**, Francis visited **Geneva**. The occasion was the 70th anniversary of the **World Council of Churches**. In this council many Orthodox, Protestant and Anglican churches work together. The Pope prayed with their representatives and also celebrated a Mass in Geneva.

Pope Francis died in **2025**, on Easter Monday. He was not buried in St Peter's Basilica but in the church of **Santa Maria Maggiore** in Rome. He had often visited this church of Our Lady. His tomb is plain, as he had wished.

gewusst: Francis was the first Pope in over 1200 years who did not come from Europe.
For the first time, a Pope chose the name Francis.

teile.einleitung: The Sermon on the Mount is the best-known speech of Jesus. It stands in the Gospel of Matthew in chapters 5 to 7. In it Jesus explains how people should live according to God's will.
wichtigste: The Sermon on the Mount is in the Gospel of Matthew, chapters 5 to 7.
It begins with the Beatitudes, which start with “Blessed are”.
The peacemakers will be called children of God.
With the images of salt and light, Jesus calls on people to do visible good.
In the Sermon on the Mount Jesus teaches the Lord's Prayer.
It contains the Golden Rule.
It ends with the image of the house on rock or sand.

abschnitte.text: According to Matthew's account, Jesus spoke to many people on a mountain. The speech begins with the **Beatitudes**. These are sentences that begin with “**Blessed are**”. Blessed means roughly happy with God. Jesus praises, for example, the meek, the merciful and those who mourn. Of the **peacemakers** he says: they will be called **children of God**.

Jesus says to his listeners: “You are the **salt of the earth**” and “You are the **light of the world**”. Salt gives food its taste, light drives away the darkness. With these images he calls on them to **bring about visible good** in the world. You do not put a light under a bucket, but so that it shines for everyone.

In one part of the speech Jesus says several times: “**You have heard that it was said ... But I say to you**”. This form is called the **antitheses**. With it Jesus sharpens well-known commandments. It is not enough to kill no one: you should not deal with others in anger either. Best known is the call even to **love your enemies**.

abschnitte.titel: The Lord's Prayer and the Golden Rule
abschnitte.text: In the Sermon on the Mount Jesus teaches the **Lord's Prayer**, the most important prayer of Christians. Then comes the **Golden Rule**: “Whatever you wish that others would do to you, do also to them.” Other religions and philosophies know similar rules. It is regarded as a simple guideline for acting well.

The Sermon on the Mount ends with an image: whoever hears the words and acts on them is like a person who builds a **house on rock**. Whoever only hears them builds a **house on sand**, which collapses in the storm. The speech has influenced many people. The theologian **Dietrich Bonhoeffer** published a book about it in 1937, **“The Cost of Discipleship”**.

gewusst: In the Gospel of Luke there is a similar, shorter speech. It is called the “Sermon on the Plain”, because Jesus speaks there on a level place.
At the Sea of Galilee there is a church on the “Mount of Beatitudes”.

teile.einleitung: The parable of the Good Samaritan is a well-known story that Jesus tells in the Gospel of Luke. It is about who is a good neighbour. The story shows that helping matters more than background or standing.
wichtigste: A man is attacked on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho.
A priest and a Levite pass by without helping.
A Samaritan treats the wounds with oil and wine.
He takes the man to an inn and gives the innkeeper two silver coins.
With this Jesus answers the question “Who is my neighbour?”.
In Switzerland, first-aid societies are called Samaritan societies.

abschnitte.titel: The question of the teacher of the law
abschnitte.text: A **teacher of the law** asked Jesus what he must do to gain eternal life. The answer was: love God and love your neighbour as yourself. Then the man asked further: “**Who is my neighbour?**” In reply Jesus told a **parable**, that is, a story with a message.

A man was travelling **from Jerusalem to Jericho**. The road runs steeply through a lonely region. Robbers **attacked** him, took everything from him and left him lying injured. First a **priest** came by, but he went on. Then came a **Levite**, a helper in the Temple. He did not help either.

At last a **Samaritan** came. The Samaritans were a people with whom many Jews were at odds at that time. But it was he who felt pity. He poured **oil and wine** on the wounds and bandaged them. Then he put the man on his own animal and brought him to an **inn**. To the innkeeper he gave **two silver coins** and promised to pay anything more later.

At the end Jesus asked: which of the three was a neighbour to the man who was attacked? The teacher of the law answered: the one who helped him. Jesus said: “**Go and do likewise!**” The story teaches that every person who needs help is our neighbour. It does not matter where someone comes from.

The word “Samaritan” stands today for people who help others in need. In Switzerland there are many **Samaritan societies**. They give **first aid** at festivals and sporting events and offer courses. Many young people attend the emergency aid course there that is needed for a driving licence.

gewusst: Many hospitals and aid organisations around the world bear the name “Samaritan”.
The two silver coins were denarii. A denarius was roughly a day's wages at that time.

teile.einleitung: Esther is a woman from the Bible. She became queen in Persia and saved her Jewish people from a dangerous plot. Her story is found in the Book of Esther.
wichtigste: Esther was a young Jewish woman who became queen.
Her cousin Mordecai had brought her up.
Haman wanted to have all the Jews in the kingdom killed.
Esther went to the king uninvited, even though this was dangerous.
She invited the king and Haman to a banquet.
The Jewish festival of Purim recalls Esther.

abschnitte.text: The story is set in the **Persian Empire**. The king was called Ahasuerus in the Bible. Esther was a young Jewish woman. Her parents had died, so her cousin **Mordecai** brought her up. The king chose Esther as his wife, and she became **queen**. At first she told no one that she was Jewish.

**Haman** was a powerful man at the king's court. Everyone was to bow before him. Mordecai did not. Haman was so angry about this that he wanted to have all the Jews in the kingdom killed. He received the king's permission for it. He fixed the day by drawing lots.

Mordecai asked Esther to plead with the king for her people. This was dangerous: anyone who went to the king **uninvited** could be punished by death. Esther and her people fasted for **three days**. Then Esther went to the king. He received her kindly.

Esther invited the king and Haman to a **banquet**. There she told the king of Haman's plan and that she herself was Jewish. The king became angry, and Haman was punished. The Jews were allowed to defend themselves and were saved. Mordecai was given a high office.

The Jewish festival of **Purim** recalls the rescue. The name comes from “pur”, which means lot. In the synagogue the Book of Esther is read aloud. When the name Haman is spoken, the children make noise with rattles. Many people dress up, rather like at carnival.

gewusst: In the Hebrew version of the Book of Esther, the word “God” does not appear even once.
Esther's Hebrew name in the Bible is Hadassah, which means myrtle.

teile.einleitung: In the parable of the mustard seed, Jesus compares the **kingdom of God** to a tiny seed. From this small seed grows a large plant in which birds nest. The message is: great things can grow from small ones.
wichtigste: The mustard seed is described as the smallest of all seeds.
A person sows it in his garden.
From it grows a large plant in whose branches birds nest.
Jesus compares the mustard seed to the kingdom of God.
The parable is found in three Gospels.
Right next to it is the parable of the yeast.

abschnitte.text: In the parable, a person takes a **mustard seed** and sows it in his **garden**. The mustard seed is described as the **smallest of all seeds**. It is only about the size of a pinhead. Even so, a **large plant** grows from it. It becomes so big that **birds** build nests in its branches.

Jesus says that the **kingdom of God** is like this mustard seed. In the beginning the movement around Jesus was very small, and only a few people followed him. But it was to grow and spread. The parable teaches: **great things can grow from small ones**. Even small good deeds can achieve a lot.

Right next to the mustard seed in the Bible is the short parable of the **yeast**. A woman mixes a little leaven into a lot of flour until the whole dough has risen. Here too, something small acts on something large. The parable of the mustard seed is in **three Gospels**: in Matthew, Mark and Luke.

From the seeds of the mustard plant, the condiment **mustard** is made. For this the seeds are ground and mixed with water, vinegar and salt. In another place Jesus says that faith as small as a mustard seed can **move mountains**. What is meant is that even a small but genuine faith has great power.

gewusst: Mustard plants belong to the same plant family as cabbage and rape.
In the Mediterranean region a mustard plant can grow as tall as a man.

teile.einleitung: Noah's Ark is a well-known story from the Bible. At God's command, Noah built a huge ship of wood. In it he saved his family and many animals from a mighty flood, the Flood.
wichtigste: At God's command Noah built a large ship, the ark.
The ark was made of wood and had three decks.
Noah took two of most animals with him.
It rained for 40 days and 40 nights.
Noah was 600 years old when the Flood came.
The ark came to rest in the mountains of Ararat.
Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.

abschnitte.text: The Bible tells that God said to **Noah** that he should build an **ark**. This was a huge ship. God told Noah to build the ark of **wood**. It had **three decks** and a door in the side. Noah obeyed and built the ship, although no rain was yet to be seen.

Noah went into the ark with his family. This included his wife, his **three sons** **Shem**, **Ham** and **Japheth** and their wives. Of most animals **two of each** went into the ark, a male and a female. In this way there could be many animals again after the flood. Many pictures show the animals going into the ship in long rows.

Then came an enormous flood that covered the whole land. This flood is called the **Flood**. In German the word originally means “great, mighty flood”. The Bible tells that it rained for **40 days and 40 nights**. The number 40 comes up often in the Bible. Noah was **600 years** old at the time. In the old stories of the Bible, people often live to a very great age.

When the water fell, the ark came to rest in the mountains of **Ararat**. A mountain with this name lies in **Turkey** today. Noah sent birds out to see whether the land was dry. A **dove** came back with an **olive branch**. A little more than a year after the start of the flood, the earth was dry, and everyone was allowed to leave the ark.

After the flood God promised never again to send such a flood. As a sign of this promise he set the **rainbow** in the sky. Similar flood stories exist in other ancient cultures too, for example in the **Epic of Gilgamesh** from Mesopotamia. The dove with the olive branch is today a world-famous sign of **peace**.

gewusst: At over 5,100 metres, Ararat is the highest mountain in Turkey.
According to the Bible the ark was 300 cubits long, which is about 150 metres.

teile.einleitung: The entry into Jerusalem is a story from the Gospels. Jesus rides into the city on a young donkey, and the people cheer him. Christians remember it on Palm Sunday, a week before Easter.
wichtigste: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a young donkey.
According to Mark, no one had ever sat on the donkey before.
Two disciples untied the donkey in a village and brought it to Jesus.
Jesus came from the Mount of Olives, which lies east of Jerusalem.
The people laid their clothes and branches on the road.
With the donkey, Jesus showed that he comes as a king of peace.
After that, Jesus drove the traders out of the Temple.

abschnitte.text: Jesus was on his way to **Jerusalem** with his disciples. He sent two disciples to a village. There they were to find a young **donkey** tied up, on which, according to **Mark**, no one had ever sat. The disciples **untied it** and brought it to Jesus. They laid their cloaks on the donkey, and Jesus sat on it.

Jesus came from the **Mount of Olives**, which lies east of Jerusalem. Many people spread their **clothes** and **branches** on the road. That was how a king was welcomed at the time. They shouted “**Hosanna**” and praised Jesus. Some **Pharisees** wanted Jesus to silence the crowd. Jesus answered that then the **stones would cry out**.

At that time a **horse** was an animal for war. But Jesus rode on a **donkey**, a simple and peaceful mount. In this way he showed that he comes as a **king of peace**. The Gospels see in this the fulfilment of a prophet's word from the Book of Zechariah. According to **Luke**, Jesus wept when he saw the city before him, because he knew that hard times were coming for it.

In Jerusalem Jesus went into the **Temple**. There people were trading and changing money. Jesus overturned the tables of the traders and **drove them out**. He said that God's house should be a **house of prayer**. This story is also called the **cleansing of the Temple**.

Christians remember the entry on **Palm Sunday**, the Sunday before Easter. With it **Holy Week** begins. According to the Gospel of John, the branches on the road were palm branches, hence the name. In many Catholic congregations in Switzerland, **palm bunches** of branches are blessed on this day. Some churches also hold a procession.

gewusst: “Hosanna” comes from Hebrew and was originally a cry for help, later a cry of joy.
In some places, a wooden donkey with a figure of Jesus used to be pulled through the streets, the Palmesel.

teile.einleitung: Trinity Sunday is a Christian feast one week after Pentecost. It celebrates the belief in one God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. In Protestant churches it is often called Trinitatis.
wichtigste: Trinity Sunday is the Sunday after Pentecost.
God is celebrated as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
In Protestant churches the feast is called Trinitatis, from the Latin “trinitas”, threefoldness.
Pope John XXII prescribed the feast for the whole Church in 1334.
A common symbol is the triangle.
Saint Patrick is said to have explained the Trinity with a shamrock.

abschnitte.text: **Trinity Sunday** follows one week after **Pentecost**. With it the Easter season comes to an end. Because Easter is on a different date every year, this feast moves too. It always falls in May or June. A few days later, on the Thursday, Catholics celebrate **Corpus Christi**.

Christians believe in **one God** who shows himself as **Father**, **Son** and **Holy Spirit**. This teaching is called the **Trinity**. It is not easy to understand, which is why there are many images for it. An important basis is the **baptismal command** in the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 28, verse 19. There Jesus sends out the disciples to baptise in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

In some regions the feast was already celebrated in the early Middle Ages. It was prescribed for the whole Church by Pope **John XXII** in the year **1334**. In **Protestant churches** the day is called **Trinitatis**, from the Latin word “trinitas”, threefoldness. The following Sundays there are counted as “Sundays after Trinity” until the autumn.

A common symbol is the equilateral **triangle**, often with an eye in it. Its three equal sides together form one unity. According to legend, Saint **Patrick** explained the Trinity to the people of **Ireland** with a **shamrock**: three leaves and yet one plant. That is why the shamrock is a symbol of Ireland today.

gewusst: In many places in Austria and southern Germany, Trinity columns stand in the squares.
The eye in the triangle can also be found on the back of the American one-dollar note.

teile.einleitung: The biblical canon is the list of writings that belong to the Bible. This list did not arise all at once but grew over centuries. Jews, Catholics and Protestants count the books in partly different ways.
wichtigste: The Greek word “canon” originally means guideline or yardstick.
The Hebrew Bible is called the Tanakh and consists of the Torah, Nevi'im and Ketuvim.
By the Jewish count the Tanakh comprises 24 books.
In the year 367 Athanasius of Alexandria named exactly the 27 writings of the New Testament.
The Council of Trent fixed the Catholic canon in 1546.
Luther called the Letter of James “an epistle of straw”.

abschnitte.text: The Greek word **canon** originally means **guideline** or **yardstick**. In the Church it describes the list of writings that count as Holy Scripture. These books are binding for faith. For a long time it was not entirely clear which writings belong to it. In the first centuries there was a lot of discussion about this.

The **Hebrew Bible** is called the **Tanakh**. The word is made up of the initial letters of its three parts: **Torah** (instruction), **Nevi'im** (prophets) and **Ketuvim** (writings). By the Jewish count the Tanakh comprises **24 books**. Christians call these writings the Old Testament, but count them differently, so that more books come out.

Around **AD 144**, **Marcion** created a collection of his own from a shortened Gospel of Luke and ten letters of Paul. He rejected the Old Testament. The Church rejected his teaching and thought harder about the canon. An early Latin list is the **Muratorian Fragment**, named after its discoverer. In the year **367**, **Athanasius of Alexandria** named for the first time, in an Easter letter, exactly the **27 writings** of the present-day New Testament.

The church historian **Eusebius of Caesarea** distinguished between accepted and disputed writings. The disputed ones he called **Antilegomena**. Doubts arose later too: in 1522 **Martin Luther** described the **Letter of James** as “an epistle of straw”. He found that this letter spoke too little of Christ. Even so, the letter stayed in his Bible.

The Catholic Church counts some books as part of the Old Testament that are not in the Tanakh, such as **Tobit** and **Judith**. The **Council of Trent** fixed this canon as binding in **1546**. For the Old Testament the Protestant churches follow the Hebrew extent. The additional books they call the **Apocrypha**, while Catholics speak of deuterocanonical books.

gewusst: The New Testament has the same 27 writings for Catholics, Orthodox and Protestants.
In his Bible, Luther put the Apocrypha in an appendix of their own between the Old and New Testaments.

teile.einleitung: In South Korea, Christianity plays a large role. The Catholic Church came into being there in an unusual way, without missionaries. Today South Korea has many Protestants and some of the largest congregations in the world.
wichtigste: The Catholic Church in Korea was founded in the 18th century by lay people without missionaries.
Andrew Kim Taegon was the first Korean Catholic priest.
In 1984 Pope John Paul II declared 103 Korean martyrs saints in Seoul.
In 1885 the missionaries Underwood and Appenzeller arrived as Protestant pioneers.
According to the 2015 census, Protestants were the largest religious community.
The Yoido Full Gospel Church in Seoul is regarded as the largest single Pentecostal congregation in the world.

abschnitte.text: In the 18th century, Korean scholars read Christian books that came from China. They studied them and began to live the faith themselves. In this way the Catholic Church in Korea was founded by **lay people without missionaries**. This is something special in the history of the Church. Priests only came to the country later.

The rulers of Korea saw the new faith as a danger. In the 19th century many Christians were persecuted and killed. Among them was **Andrew Kim Taegon**, the **first Korean Catholic priest**. He died in 1846. In **1984**, during a visit to Seoul, Pope **John Paul II** declared **103** Korean martyrs saints, including Andrew Kim Taegon.

In **1885** the two American missionaries **Underwood** and **Appenzeller** came to Korea. They are regarded as pioneers of the Protestant churches there. They founded schools and helped to build hospitals. Protestantism then grew strongly. According to the South Korean census of **2015**, **Protestants** were the largest religious community, ahead of Buddhists and Catholics.

In the capital **Seoul** there are many churches, and at night red crosses glow on some rooftops. The **Yoido Full Gospel Church** is regarded as the **largest single Pentecostal congregation in the world**. The bishop's church of the Catholic Archdiocese of Seoul is the **Myeongdong Cathedral**. It was built of brick in the Gothic style at the end of the 19th century.

gewusst: In the 2015 census, more than half of the people in South Korea said they did not belong to any religion.
Pope Francis visited South Korea in 2014.

teile.einleitung: The Armenian Apostolic Church is one of the oldest Christian churches in the world. According to tradition, Armenia became the first Christian state in the year 301. The Church has its own customs and its own script for its Bible.
wichtigste: According to tradition, King Tiridates III made Armenia a Christian state in 301.
Gregory the Illuminator is regarded as the missionary of Armenia and its first Catholicos.
The seat of the Catholicos of All Armenians is Etchmiadzin.
The Church belongs to the Oriental Orthodox churches.
Mesrop Mashtots created the Armenian alphabet around 405.
The Church traces itself back to the apostles Thaddaeus and Bartholomew.
It celebrates Christmas on 6 January.

abschnitte.text: According to tradition, the apostles **Thaddaeus** and **Bartholomew** already preached in Armenia in the 1st century. That is why the Church calls itself **“apostolic”**. According to tradition, King **Tiridates III** raised Christianity to the state religion in the year **301**. Armenia would thus be the **first Christian state** in the world. Some scholars date this rather to the year 314.

**Gregory the Illuminator** is regarded as the missionary of Armenia. He is said to have been held prisoner in a pit for years. Then he healed the king and converted him to Christianity. Gregory became the first **Catholicos**, as the head of the Church is called. The Church is sometimes also called **“Gregorian”** after him.

The seat of the **Catholicos of All Armenians** is **Etchmiadzin**, west of the capital **Yerevan**. The cathedral of Etchmiadzin is regarded as one of the oldest cathedrals in the world. There is also the **Catholicosate of the Great House of Cilicia**. It arose in the medieval kingdom of Cilicia and has had its seat in **Antelias** near Beirut in Lebanon since **1930**.

Around the year **405**, **Mesrop Mashtots** created the **Armenian alphabet**. He wanted the Armenians to be able to read the Bible in their own language. The Catholicos **Sahak** helped him. Soon afterwards the Armenian translation of the Bible was made. The alphabet is still used today and is an important part of Armenian culture.

abschnitte.titel: A church family of its own
abschnitte.text: Like the **Coptic** and the **Ethiopian** churches, the Armenian Church did not recognise the **Council of Chalcedon** of **451**. That is why it belongs to the **Oriental Orthodox churches**. It has kept an old custom: it celebrates the birth and the baptism of Jesus together on **6 January**. The Patriarchate in Jerusalem follows the Julian calendar and therefore celebrates on 19 January.

gewusst: There are Armenian congregations in Switzerland too, with a church in Troinex near Geneva.
Many Armenians live outside Armenia, for example in Russia, France and the USA.

teile.einleitung: A hymn book is a book of **songs for church services**. So that everyone can sing together, it is available in many churches. Alongside the words there is often also the musical notation of the tune.
wichtigste: The hymn book contains the songs for the service.
Every hymn has a number, so you can find it quickly.
The hymn numbers are shown at the front on a hymn board.
Songs for the service are called church hymns.
The musical notes are often above the words.
The hymn books are usually available in the pews.

abschnitte.titel: What is in the hymn book
abschnitte.text: A hymn book contains many **church hymns**, that is, songs sung in the service. Some are already several hundred years old, others are quite new. Often the **notes** are above the words, so you can see how the tune goes. Many hymn books also contain prayers and texts from the Bible. The songs are usually arranged by church year or by theme.

Every hymn has its own **number** in the hymn book. At the front of the church hangs a **hymn board**. Before the service the numbers of the hymns are put up there. That way everyone knows straight away which page to turn to. The hymn books are often available in the **church pews** or at the entrance and are put back afterwards.

Even in the Bible there is a book of songs: the **Psalms**. There are 150 songs and prayers. Many of them are attributed to **King David**, who is said to have loved playing the harp. In the Reformed churches, Psalms used to be sung especially often, for example in the Geneva Psalter.

Since the **Reformation**, the whole congregation has sung along in the service, not just a choir. For this, books with songs for everyone were needed. In German-speaking Switzerland today there are, for example, the **Reformed Hymn Book** and the **Catholic Hymn Book**. Many songs are in both books, because they are sung by all Christians.

gewusst: Some church hymns that are still sung today were written by Martin Luther and are almost 500 years old.
The invention of printing first made it possible for many people to have their own hymn book.

teile.einleitung: The Anglican Church came into being in England when the Church separated from Rome in the 16th century. Its mother church is the Church of England. Today there are Anglican churches on all continents.
wichtigste: King Henry VIII separated the Church of England from Rome in 1534.
The British monarch is formally the secular head of the Church of England.
The most important clergyman is the Archbishop of Canterbury.
The well-known prayer book is called the Book of Common Prayer.
British kings are crowned in Westminster Abbey.
In the USA the Anglican church is called the Episcopal Church.
The worldwide union is called the Anglican Communion.

abschnitte.text: King **Henry VIII** of England wanted to have his marriage annulled. The **pope** refused. The king then separated the Church of England from Rome. With the **Act of Supremacy** of **1534** he made himself the head of the Church of England. In this way the **Church of England** came into being.

Since the Reformation the **king** or **queen** has formally stood at the head of the Church of England. The title is **Supreme Governor**. In 2026 this is King **Charles III**. The most important clergyman, however, is the **Archbishop of Canterbury**. He is the highest-ranking bishop of the Church of England and is regarded as the spiritual centre of Anglicans worldwide.

The famous prayer book of the Anglicans is called the **Book of Common Prayer**. It first appeared in **1549** and goes back to Archbishop **Thomas Cranmer**. It brought worship in the **English language** instead of Latin. Many prayers from it are still well known in English today. The Anglican Church combines Catholic traditions with ideas of the Reformation.

In **Westminster Abbey** in London, British kings have been crowned since **1066**. The abbey is an Anglican church. King **Charles III** was also crowned there in **2023**. In Westminster Abbey many kings and famous figures are also buried.

The worldwide union of Anglican churches is called the **Anglican Communion**. It unites 42 independent church provinces and further churches on all continents. Many of them arose in former **British colonies**, for example in Africa. In the **USA** the Anglicans call themselves the **Episcopal Church**, because they are led by bishops. The Latin word for bishops is “episcopi”.

gewusst: In Switzerland too there are Anglican congregations with services in English, for example in Zurich, Bern and Geneva.
In the Church of England, priests may marry, and since 2014 women can also become bishops.

teile.einleitung: Ordination of women means that women are appointed to a spiritual office, for example as a pastor or priest. The churches handle this very differently. In Switzerland the first women pastors existed as early as 1918.
wichtigste: “Ordination” is the appointment to a spiritual office.
In 1918 the first women in Switzerland were ordained as pastors in Zurich.
Since 1963 women in the Reformed church of Zurich have been allowed to work fully as pastors.
In 1994 John Paul II declared that the Church could not ordain women as priests.
Since 2000 the Christ Catholic Church has also ordained women as priests.
In 1992 Maria Jepsen became the first Lutheran woman bishop in the world, in Hamburg.

abschnitte.text: With **ordination**, a person is appointed to a **spiritual office**. They may then, for example, preach, baptise and lead the Lord's Supper. In the Catholic and Orthodox churches this is called **consecration**. Whether women may also be ordained is answered differently by the churches.

abschnitte.titel: The first women pastors in Zurich
abschnitte.text: In **1918** the first women in Switzerland were ordained as pastors in **Zurich**. But they were not allowed to take on a parish post. In 1921 the Zurich cantonal government rejected their eligibility. Its reason was that **women had no right to vote**, so they could not be elected either. Only since **1963** have women in the Reformed church of the canton of Zurich been legally allowed to work fully as pastors.

In many Protestant churches, women are now naturally pastors. In **1992** **Maria Jepsen** became the first Lutheran **woman bishop** in the world, in Hamburg. In Switzerland, **Rita Famos** became the first president of the Evangelical Reformed Church of Switzerland in 2021. The **Christ Catholic Church** of Switzerland separated from Rome in the 19th century. Since **2000** it has also ordained women as priests.

In the Catholic Church only men are ordained as priests. In 1994, in the letter **“Ordinatio sacerdotalis”**, Pope **John Paul II** declared that the Church has no authority to ordain women as priests. He justified this by saying that Jesus chose only men as apostles. Many Catholics, including in Switzerland, wish for a change. Others hold to the existing teaching. The Orthodox churches also do not ordain women.

gewusst: The first two Zurich women pastors of 1918 were called Elise Pfister and Rosa Gutknecht.
In Switzerland, women's suffrage at federal level was only introduced in 1971.

teile.einleitung: The Fraumünster is a famous church in the old town of Zurich. It stands on the Limmat opposite the Grossmünster. Its coloured glass windows by Marc Chagall are known all over the world.
wichtigste: The Fraumünster stands in Zurich.
King Louis the German founded a convent for women here in 853.
The last abbess, Katharina von Zimmern, handed the convent over to the city in 1524.
In the choir there are five glass windows by Marc Chagall.
The middle Christ window is mainly green.
Augusto Giacometti created the large window in the north transept in 1945.

abschnitte.text: In the year **853**, King **Louis the German** founded a **convent for women** in Zurich. His daughter Hildegard became the first abbess. An abbess is the head of a women's convent. The convent was very powerful for a long time. The abbesses at times had important rights in Zurich, for example the right to mint coins.

In the time of the **Reformation**, much changed in Zurich. In 1524 the last abbess, **Katharina von Zimmern**, handed the convent over to the **city of Zurich**. In this way she prevented conflict and violence. The Fraumünster then became a Reformed church, and it is one to this day.

The artist **Marc Chagall** created **five** large glass windows for the choir of the Fraumünster. They were inaugurated in 1970. They show stories from the Bible. The middle one is the **Christ window**, and it glows mainly **green**. Chagall came from a **Jewish family** in Russia, in what is now Belarus. Many of his pictures show figures from the Bible.

As early as **1945** the Swiss artist **Augusto Giacometti** created the large window in the **north transept**. It is very tall and colourful. Later Chagall also designed a rose window in the south transept. Every day many visitors come to see the windows.

gewusst: Chagall was already over 80 years old when he created the windows for the Fraumünster.
Augusto Giacometti was a relative of the famous sculptor Alberto Giacometti.

teile.einleitung: Army chaplaincy looks after the spiritual concerns of soldiers. Army chaplains listen, advise and help in difficult situations. In the Swiss Army this task has existed for a very long time.
wichtigste: In the past, army chaplains in Switzerland were called field preachers.
Since 2004 they have officially been called army chaplains.
They are there for all members of the army, regardless of religion and worldview.
Army chaplains hold the rank of captain.
The conversations are confidential.
At the start of the 2020s, army chaplaincy opened up to Jewish and Muslim communities.

abschnitte.text: In **military service** many people are far away from home. Some are homesick, have worries in the family or problems on duty. Then they can turn to the **army chaplaincy**. The chaplains listen, advise and help further. The conversations are **confidential**. Army chaplaincy is an offer for everyone, from the recruit to the commander.

abschnitte.titel: From field preacher to army chaplain
abschnitte.text: In the past the chaplains in the Swiss Army were called **field preachers**. They held services and were responsible for all soldiers, regardless of denomination. With the **Army XXI** reform the name was changed in **2004**. Since then they have been called **army chaplains**. The new name stresses **pastoral care**, that is, accompanying people, rather than preaching.

Army chaplains hold the military rank of **captain**. But they stand **outside the normal chain of command**. This is important so that the soldiers can trust them. What someone says is not passed on to superiors. Army chaplaincy is there for **all members of the army**, regardless of religion and worldview.

For almost **140 years** the **national churches** alone provided army chaplaincy, that is, the Reformed, the Catholic and the Christian Catholic Church. At the start of the **2020s**, **free churches** as well as **Jewish** and **Muslim** chaplains were added. In this way army chaplaincy reflects better how diverse Switzerland is today. At the start of 2022 around **170** army chaplains were in service.

gewusst: With Army Revision 23, the number of army chaplains was meant to rise to about 240.
Many other countries also have a chaplaincy for their army.

teile.einleitung: The Three Kings' cake belongs to 6 January, Epiphany, in Switzerland. A small figure of a king is hidden in one piece. Whoever finds it is king or queen for a day.
wichtigste: The Three Kings' cake is eaten on Epiphany, 6 January.
In one piece there is a small figure of a king, usually made of plastic.
Whoever finds the figure becomes king or queen for a day.
The cake usually comes with a golden paper crown.
The Swiss cake is made of sweet yeast dough and consists of balls like a blossom.
Max Währen made the custom well known again in the 1950s.
In France people eat the Galette des Rois.

abschnitte.text: On **6 January** Christians remember the **wise men from the East**. According to the Gospel of Matthew they followed a star to the newborn Jesus. They brought **gold, frankincense and myrrh** as gifts. Later they were called kings and given the names **Caspar, Melchior and Balthazar**. On their feast day in Switzerland, people bake or buy a Three Kings' cake.

The **Swiss Three Kings' cake** is baked from sweet **yeast dough**, like a plait loaf. Around one large **ball** in the middle lie several small balls. Together they look like a **blossom**. On top people often sprinkle **pearl sugar** and flaked almonds. Some cakes also contain raisins.

In one of the pieces of cake there is a small **figure of a king**, usually made of plastic. Everyone hopes to find it. Whoever gets the piece with the figure becomes **king or queen** for a day. He or she may put on the golden **paper crown** that comes with the cake. Often the king may then also decide something. When eating, of course, you have to bite carefully.

The custom is old, but in Switzerland it had almost been forgotten. In the **1950s** the bread researcher **Max Währen** revived it. Bakeries joined in, and soon the cake was popular all over the country. Today Swiss bakeries and shops sell very many Three Kings' cakes around 6 January.

There are cakes for Epiphany elsewhere too. In **France** people eat the **Galette des Rois**, the “cake of the kings”. In the north of France it is often made of **puff pastry** with an almond filling. In Spain the cake is called “Roscón de Reyes” and is ring-shaped. Everywhere the same applies: whoever finds the hidden figure is lucky.

gewusst: In the past, a dried bean was often hidden in the cake instead of a figure.
In French-speaking Switzerland, the Galette des Rois is also known alongside the Three Kings' cake.
